job.title: Recruitment - Government Recruitment and Selection
job.description:
About the Opportunity

Beilby Downing Teal has partnered with the WA public sector in delivering trusted recruitment and HR solutions for over 25 years. Due to unprecedented growth, we are now seeking experienced Recruitment Consultants to join our Perth Government Practice to work with government agencies in selecting suitably skilled staff through an objective and robust section process.

This is an opportunity to play a trusted, independent role, working with selection panels  in ensuring candidate evidence, panel deliberations and appointment recommendations are documented accurately, objectively and professionally.

You will work across varied assignments, from shortlisting and interviews through to referee checks and final selection reports ensuring selection panels reach defensible, merit-based decisions in accordance with the Public Sector Management Act and Commissioners Instructions.
The main function of your role will be to:
  • Facilitate panel briefings, shortlisting meetings, interviews and final deliberations.
  • Capture accurate, objective notes of candidate evidence and panel discussions.
  • Guide panels in applying approved selection criteria consistently and in accordance with internal policies.
  • Prepare shortlisting matrices, interview summaries, referee-check records and selection reports.
  • Document comparative assessments, conclusions and recommendations clearly.
  • Incorporate feedback and finalise high-quality documents within agreed deadlines.
  • Maintain strict confidentiality, impartiality and secure information handling.
About you

We are seeking experienced recruitment consultants with a good understanding of the WA Public Sector Management Act and merit-based recruitment.

We would love to hear from you if you have:
  • Experience supporting government or public sector recruitment and selection processes.
  • Excellent writing, note-taking, analytical and report-preparation skills.
  • A sound understanding of merit, equity, procedural fairness and confidentiality.
  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to work independently and accurately under pressure.
  • Professional judgement and confidence working with senior panel members.
  • Responsiveness, discretion and the ability to meet tight deadlines.
Highly regarded
  • Knowledge of relevant government employment frameworks and recruitment policies.
  • Experience in job classification / design.
  • Experience with executive, specialist, bulk or high-volume recruitment.
Why work with us?

These roles offer flexible, assignment-based hours rather than a fixed weekly schedule. You can choose assignments and working hours that suit your availability, provided you can meet the agreed client requirements and deadlines.
Working primarily from your home office, you will enjoy autonomy, exposure to a broad range of government recruitment processes and the opportunity to contribute to fair and transparent public sector appointments.
Each engagement includes a clear brief, agreed templates and defined deliverables, with support from an experienced administration team and supportive colleagues.

Apply now

If you are an experienced public sector recruitment professional with exceptional writing skills and a commitment to impartiality, we would welcome your application. 
Please apply online at www.beilbydt.com.au by submitting a cover letter and resume (Word or PDF format) and quoting reference number 1257038.
For further information, please contact Denise Wetherall, National General Manager – Government on 0408 000 109 or dwetherall@beilbydt.com.au

job.title: Chief Executive Officer - Western Australian Meat Industry Authority
job.description:
Chief Executive Officer - Western Australian Meat Industry Authority
Employment type: Fixed Term - Full Time
Branch: MLC
Levels: Class 2
Region: Wheatbelt Region, Western Australia
Closing at: Oct 26 2026 - 16:00 AWST
Classification: Class 2 $222,530 p.a. PSCA 2024
Location: Muchea
  
Lead an Industry. Influence Government. Drive Sustainable Growth.
 
A rare executive opportunity requiring the strategic agility to navigate government and the commercial acumen to deliver sustainable business outcomes.

The Western Australian Meat Industry Authority (WAMIA) is seeking an exceptional leader to serve as its next Chief Executive Officer.
Established under the Western Australian Meat Industry Authority Act 1976, WAMIA plays a unique role within Western Australia's meat and livestock sector. As an independent statutory authority, WAMIA provides strategic advice to Government, regulates the meat processing industry and owns and operates the Muchea Livestock Centre, one of Australia's leading livestock exchange facilities.
This is a rare opportunity to lead a public sector organisation with significant industry influence, commercial operations and direct engagement with Government, Ministers, industry stakeholders and regional communities.

The Opportunity

Reporting to the WAMIA Board, the CEO will provide strategic leadership across the Authority's regulatory, policy and commercial responsibilities, ensuring the organisation delivers on its legislative functions while positioning itself for long-term sustainability and growth.
Success in this role will require the ability to confidently navigate government processes, work effectively within a Board-governed environment and build productive relationships across Ministers' offices, government agencies, industry bodies and commercial stakeholders.
The CEO will lead organisational strategy and reform, oversee the operation of the Muchea Livestock Centre, provide high-level policy advice to Government and drive initiatives that support a thriving and sustainable meat and livestock industry in Western Australia.
Equally important is the ability to balance public sector stewardship with commercial discipline. The CEO will oversee the Authority's financial performance, identify opportunities to strengthen revenue and cost recovery, maximise returns on significant land and infrastructure assets, and ensure the organisation remains financially sustainable while delivering on its public purpose.

What We're Looking For

We are seeking an accomplished executive who brings credibility, sound judgement and a demonstrated ability to lead complex organisations operating in dynamic environments.
The successful applicant will demonstrate:
  • Significant experience working within, or closely alongside, government, including navigating public sector governance, legislative frameworks, cabinet, ministerial or parliamentary processes.
  • Strong commercial and financial management capability, including budget oversight, strategic investment decisions, financial sustainability and organisational performance.
  • Experience leading organisational strategy, reform and change in complex stakeholder environments.
  • Exceptional stakeholder engagement skills with the ability to build trusted relationships across government, industry, community and commercial sectors.
  • Strong governance experience, including working effectively with Boards and providing high-quality strategic advice.
  • A record of delivering outcomes through collaboration, negotiation and influence.
  • Personal integrity, resilience and leadership that fosters a positive, accountable and high-performing organisational culture.

Why Join WAMIA?

This is an opportunity to lead a respected statutory authority whose decisions and initiatives have a genuine impact on Western Australia's agricultural sector and regional economy.
As CEO, you will have the opportunity to:
  • Influence industry and government outcomes at a strategic level.
  • Lead a unique organisation with regulatory, policy and commercial responsibilities.
  • Shape the future direction of the Western Australian meat and livestock industry.
  • Work closely with government, industry leaders and key stakeholders across the State.
  • Drive innovation, sustainability and long-term organisational success.

Location

The Authority’s office locations are Muchea and West Perth, Western Australia. Flexible arrangements may be considered; however, the successful applicant will be expected to maintain a strong presence at Muchea and travel as required to metropolitan Perth, regional Western Australia and stakeholder meetings.

Remuneration and entitlements

This position is classified as CEO Class 2, with a salary point of $222,530 per annum, plus employer contribution to superannuation. The option to participate in the Senior Officers Vehicle Scheme is also provided to the successful candidate.

Eligibility Requirements

Appointment is subject to:
  • Eligibility to work in Australia.
  • National Police Clearance.
  • Pre-employment medical assessment.
  • Participation in WAMIA's Q Fever Vaccination Program.
  • Current driver's licence.
  • Occasional travel to regional areas of Western Australia.
  
How to Apply
To lodge your application, and view the application pack and JDF visit, Please copy and paste below link https://search.jobs.wa.gov.au/jobs/chief-executive-officer-wheatbelt-region-western-australia-australia

All Applications must be submitted through Jobs WA

To apply, please submit:
  • A current comprehensive curriculum vitae that highlights your skills, experience and achievements.
  • A cover letter of no more than two pages demonstrating how your skills, knowledge, experience and personal attributes meet the requirements of the role as outlined in the attached Job Description Form (JDF).
For further information, please contact Andrea Hancock, HR Consultant, on ahancock@beilbydt.com.au.
  
Closing date: 4pm 26 October 2026
  
Please be aware that late applications will not be accepted. It is your responsibility to ensure your application has been submitted prior to the closing date and time. If you experience technical difficulties applying online, please contact the RAMS Helpdesk on 1300 733 056.
  
Privacy and your personal information
  
WAMIA handles and releases information in accordance with relevant privacy and information access laws including the Freedom of Information Act 1992 (FOI) and the Privacy and Responsible Information Sharing Act 2024 (WA) (PRIS). Further information is available via our Privacy Statement.

job.title: Senior Field Service Engineer
job.description:
The Company

Innovation has been at the heart of our clients business since 1889 — from pioneering magnetic separation to redefining non‑ferrous metal recovery and sensor‑based sorting. Today, they combine proven technologies with data‑driven insights, empower customers to unlock new value, recover high‑quality secondary raw materials, and build highly profitable circular economies.

The Opportunity

Reporting to the National Sales Manager, the Senior Field Service Engineer will be responsible for delivering comprehensive after‑sales technical support to customers throughout the full lifecycle of their equipment. This includes installation and commissioning, planned maintenance, unplanned breakdown support, and the programming and optimisation of sorting systems.
After‑sales support may be provided either on site or remotely, including phone-based assistance and remote maintenance access to customer equipment, depending on the situation.

About you

We are seeking an experienced Senior Technician who enjoys commissioning new equipment, providing on‑site servicing, delivering technical support, and building strong customer relationships.
The ideal candidate will demonstrate experience in the following areas:
  • Strong electrical expertise, particularly in electrical control systems. A technical degree or diploma in an electrical discipline is highly regarded.
  • Proven fault‑finding and diagnostic skills, with hands‑on experience responding to and resolving breakdown situations.
  • Solid mechanical knowledge, with the ability to work confidently across electrical and mechanical systems.
  • Willingness and ability to travel regularly, sometimes at short notice, including international travel to Germany, the USA, New Zealand, and South East Asia.
  • Flexibility to work outside standard business hours on occasion, including weekends, as operational requirements demand with overtime rates provided.
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to clearly explain technical issues to internal teams and customers alike, ensuring expectations are effectively managed.
Why this role

The successful candidate will be provided an excellent compensation package including international training ( Germany ) and career growth. Interested candidates are encouraged to apply via the “Apply for this job” button or through our website at www.beilbydt.com.au, quoting reference number 1256160. For further inquiries, please contact Aaron Hooper at ahooper@beilbydt.com.au

job.title: Manager Finance - Shire of Irwin
job.description:
THE SHIRE

The Shire of Irwin is located on the stunning Batavia Coast, where the historic twin towns of Dongara and Port Denison offer an enviable lifestyle, a welcoming community and a diverse local economy positioned for sustainable growth. Home to approximately 3,800 residents and spanning 2,223 km² of coastal and rural landscapes, this is an opportunity to join a progressive local government at an important time of organisational development and community investment.

THE OPPORTUNITY

A rewarding leadership opportunity is available for an experienced finance professional who can combine strong technical capability with practical, forward-looking strategic advice. Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer and participating as a key member of the executive leadership team, the Manager Finance will help shape the organisation’s direction. The role will assess proposals, model options, challenge assumptions and advise Council, the CEO and managers on long-term financial sustainability, service delivery, major projects and investment priorities.

THE SUCCESSFUL CANDIDATE

We are seeking a confident and capable leader from a commercial, operational or local government background with:
  • A demonstrated record of providing strategic financial advice to senior leaders and governing bodies;
  • Strong experience in long-term financial planning, budgeting, forecasting and scenario modelling;
  • The ability to translate complex financial information into clear options and practical recommendations;
  • A collaborative approach to business partnering and strengthening organisation-wide financial accountability;
  • Proven experience leading and developing a capable, service-oriented finance team;
  • Tertiary qualifications in Accounting, Finance, Commerce or a related discipline, with strong knowledge of Australian Accounting Standards and the ability to rapidly acquire and apply Western Australian local government financial requirements.
The position leads budgeting, long-term financial planning, statutory reporting, rates, treasury, taxation, financial systems and internal financial controls. Day-to-day payroll administration is managed outside the Finance Department, allowing the role to focus on strategic leadership, organisational support and continuous improvement. Eligibility for CPA Australia or CA ANZ membership will be highly regarded.

THE PACKAGE

In return you will receive a three-to-five-year contract, a competitive base salary, negotiable depending on experience, plus company vehicle, additional superannuation and benefits. The successful candidate will have the option of living full time in Shire accommodation or adopting a hybrid working arrangement, providing the flexibility of working remotely for most of the time, with visiting the Shire regularly to stay connected with the team in person. This is a fantastic opportunity for someone to progress their career and join the Shire at this pivotal time.

To apply please click the Apply Now button or visit www.beilbydt.com.au quoting reference 1248622 and provide a comprehensive resume and a covering letter of no more than two pages, specifically addressing each of the six selection criteria in Section 7.0 within the Application Pack, using concise examples of relevant experience and achievements. 

Download an Application Pack by clicking or copying and pasting this link in your browser: https://beilbydt.com.au/application-packs

For initial enquiries, or for any assistance you may need in making your application, please contact Emily Bulloch for a confidential discussion on 0427 582 402 or ebulloch@beilbydt.com.au.

Applications will close at 4pm AWST on Monday 2 November 2026. The Shire reserves the right to commence the recruitment process at any time.

Canvassing Elected Members during the recruitment process will disqualify your application.

job.title: Structural Engineer
job.description:
The Company

Our client is a large-scale industrial operation responsible for the safe, reliable and efficient management of critical infrastructure supporting Australia's export supply chain. Operating a complex asset portfolio, the organisation is recognised for its strong safety culture, commitment to continuous improvement and long-term investment in engineering excellence.

With a focus on operational reliability, innovation and sustainable asset stewardship, the business provides an environment where engineers can make a genuine impact while working alongside experienced technical professionals.

The Opportunity

Reporting to the Senior Structural Engineer, this role is responsible for managing the condition, performance and integrity of structural and civil assets across a large industrial operation. The position combines technical engineering, asset integrity, project delivery and stakeholder management, ensuring critical infrastructure remains safe, reliable and fit for purpose.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Assessing structural asset condition and undertaking engineering investigations
  • Completing structural calculations, technical reports and engineering assessments
  • Developing, prioritising and coordinating repair and modification programs
  • Supporting plant inspections, risk assessments and asset integrity management activities
  • Providing technical advice to maintenance, operational and project teams
  • Managing consultants, contractors and specialist engineering suppliers
  • Contributing to shutdown planning, failure investigations and continuous improvement initiatives
  • Assisting with project budgeting, forecasting and cost management activities.
This position offers the opportunity to work across a diverse range of challenging structural assets, supporting both day-to-day operational requirements and longer-term capital improvement programs.

About You

We are seeking an engineer with strong technical capability, excellent problem-solving skills and a genuine commitment to safety and asset reliability.
To be successful, you will ideally possess:
  • Degree qualifications in Civil or Structural Engineering
  • Experience within structural engineering, asset integrity or heavy industrial environments
  • Strong analytical, investigation and technical reporting skills
  • Experience undertaking structural assessments, calculations and engineering reviews
  • Well-developed stakeholder engagement and communication skills
  • The ability to coordinate contractors, consultants and technical specialists
  • Strong planning, organisation and project management capabilities
  • Commitment to safety, compliance and continuous improvement
  • A proactive attitude and desire for ongoing professional development
Experience within bulk materials handling, mining, ports, marine infrastructure, manufacturing or other heavy industrial sectors will be highly regarded. Exposure to large dynamic machinery, asset management systems and project delivery environments would also be advantageous.

Why This Role

This is an excellent opportunity to join a highly respected industrial organisation where engineering expertise is valued and where you can play a key role in maintaining and improving critical infrastructure.

You will enjoy exposure to major structural assets, complex engineering challenges and long-term asset improvement initiatives, while working within a collaborative, safety-focused team environment that encourages professional growth and development.

For a confidential discussion, please contact Jessica O'Neill on 0457 336 833. Applications should be submitted via our website.

job.title: Operations Manager
job.description:
The Company

Northern Australia Civil is a privately owned civil services business operating throughout the Northern Territory and Western Australia.  The business provides wet hire plant and skilled labour solutions to civil, mining and infrastructure clients, while also delivering selected civil contracting works including mine site development, road construction, bulk earthworks, drainage and remote infrastructure.

With a reputation built on quality, reliability and strong client relationships, NAC has continued to grow across Northern Australia. The company’s fleet, workforce and project capability support principal contractors across challenging regional and remote environments, with a strong focus on safe, reliable and productive delivery.

The Opportunity

Reporting to the Managing Director, the Operations Manager will lead the day-to-day delivery of plant and labour hire operations across multiple client sites throughout NT and WA.

The role is responsible for coordinating plant, operators and labour resources, ensuring client commitments are delivered safely, efficiently and to a high standard. You will also support selected civil projects and drive improvements in planning, utilisation and operational performance.

Key Responsibilities:
  • Lead plant and labour hire operations across NT and WA , with travel to sites required
  • Coordinate workforce rosters, plant allocation and mobilisation
  • Manage client delivery requirements and operational issues
  • Improve scheduling, resource utilisation and operational systems
  • Lead supervisors, operators, labour hire personnel and project teams
  • Monitor utilisation, productivity and operational costs
  • Support safety, quality and compliance standards
  • Liaise with the NAC workshop regarding servicing, repairs and workforce allocation
About You

You are an experienced operational leader with a background in plant hire, labour hire, civil construction, mining or a similar industry. You bring strong commercial awareness, practical leadership skills and the ability to coordinate people, equipment and clients across multiple sites.
  
Ideally, you will have:
  • Experience in a senior operational leadership role
  • Proven ability to coordinate plant, equipment and workforce resources
  • Strong understanding of utilisation, service delivery and cost control
  • Excellent planning, organisation and problem-solving skills
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management capability
  • Good Microsoft Office skills
  • Current C Class Driver Licence and White Card
Experience in wet hire, labour hire or civil operations is key to this role. Qualifications in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, Business, Logistics or a related field will be well regarded although your years of experience and leadership skills will be equally well regarded

Why This Role

This is an opportunity to play a key leadership role within a growing business that has established civil contracting capability and a strong reputation across Northern Australia.

You will have the autonomy to lead operations, improve performance, support a capable team and contribute directly to the company's continued growth.

 For further information, please contact Mark Turner on 0401 404 451.

job.title: Director Transformation - City of Wanneroo
job.description:
About the City of Wanneroo

Home to more than 236,000 people, the City of Wanneroo is a young, diverse and rapidly growing community. With our population projected to grow by around 70% by 2046, we are actively planning for a future city of close to 500,000 residents.

From established suburbs and rapidly developing growth corridors to industrial precincts, coastal and rural communities and significant natural areas, our scale and diversity create exciting opportunities and complex challenges.

Our 1,000-plus employees are at the heart of delivering for this growing community. With a new Workforce Plan and Digital Strategy, we are investing in simpler systems and processes, better use of data and technology, and the organisational capability we will need for the decades ahead.

About the Position

Reporting directly to the CEO, the newly created Director Transformation will bring together digital, process and data transformation to shape a more scalable, efficient and effective organisation.

Leading around 70 FTE, you will align strategy, improvement, data and digital capability to drive whole-of-organisation change and deliver measurable value for our people and community.

You will also lead one of Council’s most visible commitments: providing 100% of transactional services online by 2030. This is a rare opportunity to build a new Directorate, shape its culture and capability, and leave a lasting imprint on one of Western Australia’s fastest-growing cities.

About you

We are looking for a values-driven, people-focused leader with a strong track record of enterprise-wide transformation, and the ability to bring people on the journey with you.

You will have led complex change, multidisciplinary projects and business improvement through to measurable outcomes, leaving both the organisation and your teams stronger as a result. You know how to simplify the way organisations work, build high-performing teams and turn ambitious targets into results.

If you are curious and collaborative, enjoy solving complex problems and genuinely get satisfaction from helping others do their best work, you will feel at home at the City of Wanneroo.

In Return

We are offering a contract of up to five-years, with a remuneration package of up to $330,821 per annum, comprising a base salary, superannuation (including the option to co-contribute up to 15%) and a vehicle or vehicle allowance.

We know that leaders do their best thinking when they are genuinely able to step away and recharge. This means you will receive five weeks’ annual leave, plus 12 executive leave days.

Most of all, you will join a leadership team that backs its people, welcomes fresh thinking, and is committed to making the City of Wanneroo a place where everyone can do their best work.

To apply, please click the Apply Now button or visit www.beilbydt.com.au quoting reference 1132353. Please provide a comprehensive resume and a covering letter of no more than two pages, outlining your motivation for applying and addressing your suitability for the role.

Download an Application Pack here: https://beilbydt.com.au/application-packs

For initial enquiries, or for any assistance you may need in making your application, please contact Emily Bulloch for a confidential discussion on 0427 582 402 or ebulloch@beilbydt.com.au.

Applications close at 4pm AWST on Wednesday 14 October 2026.

Please note, canvassing of Elected Members will disqualify.

job.title: Senior Accounting Officer
job.description:
About WATC

As the State’s central financial services provider, Western Australian Treasury Corporation (WATC) cares about the financial health of Western Australia’s government sector. WATC partner with government entities to achieve sound financial outcomes and provide access to a comprehensive range of corporate finance, debt and investment, risk management and foreign exchange products and advisory services. They also provide their investors with secure and sustainable opportunities.

You can find out more about the organisation including our purpose, history and key activities by visiting the About Us tab on the WATC website.

The Opportunity
WATC are seeking an experienced Senior Accounting Officer to join their Finance, Administration and Treasury Operations team. Reporting to the Finance Manager, you will take ownership of accurate and timely financial accounting activities through to trial balance, including daily reconciliations and reporting that support WATC’s operations. This permanent role suits a self-managing professional who enjoys hands-on transactional accounting, works confidently to recurring deadlines, and is motivated to contribute to a high-performing team.
Key activities include:
  • Performing daily and month-end bank reconciliations and completing the daily profit and loss reconciliation process.
  • Managing accounts receivable activities, client accounting files and foreign currency invoice approvals.
  • Coordinating month-end processes, including journals, accruals, prepayments, balance sheet reconciliations and other financial adjustments.
  • Producing accurate monthly reporting through to a completed trial balance and supporting quarterly, statutory and management reporting.
  • Maintaining the integrity of the general ledger, chart of accounts, fixed asset register and supporting accounting systems and procedures.
  • Supporting tax compliance, year-end financial statements, internal and external audits, and the application of accounting standards.
  • Contributing ideas and practical improvements to processes, documentation and team initiatives.
About You

WATC’s ideal applicant is an organised and dependable accounting professional who combines strong technical capability with a practical, collaborative approach. You will be comfortable taking ownership of recurring daily deliverables, keeping stakeholders informed and maintaining accuracy during busy reporting periods.
If you can demonstrate the following capabilities and experience, we would love to hear from you:
  • CA or CPA qualification (or equivalent) with current membership.
  • Strong technical accounting knowledge, including the interpretation and application of Australian Accounting Standards.
  • Demonstrated experience in financial accounting, reconciliations and reporting through to trial balance.
  • Intermediate to advanced Excel skills and confidence using financial accounting and related business systems.
  • Ability to organise priorities, work autonomously and provide clear assurance that key deliverables are progressing.
  • Constructive and professional communication skills, with the confidence to work closely with the Finance Manager and a range of internal stakeholders.
  • A collaborative mindset, sound judgement and a genuine interest in improving efficiency, quality and productivity.
WATC Values

WATC values shape their behaviours and define how they relate to each other, their clients and their community:
Integrity – We are open, honest and accountable. We adhere to the highest professional and ethical standards. We honour our promises.
Partnership – We work collaboratively with our stakeholders and colleagues towards achieving successful outcomes.
Adaptability – We challenge ourselves to think creatively and to continuously improve.
Achievement – We are engaged and focused on delivering valued outcomes for Western Australia.
Leadership – We use our knowledge and experience to contribute to the long-term benefit of Western Australia.
Employee Benefits WATC offer a range of benefits beyond remuneration that include:
  • Flexible work arrangements:
    • A supportive approach to work / life balance
    • Working from home options and flexible start and finish times
    • Compressed work schedules and part-time work opportunities.
  • Health and wellbeing focus:
    • Calendar of a range of wellbeing initiatives
    • Two wellbeing days annually
    • Discounted health insurance.
  • Generous leave:
    • 12.5 days personal leave per year
    • Up to 12 weeks paid parental leave (on top of government paid parental leave scheme)
    • Access to purchase additional annual leave.
  • Diverse, inclusive and supportive work environment:
    • Strong organisational focus on diversity and inclusion
    • A reward and recognition program.
  • Professional development opportunities:
    • Professional memberships
    • Support for tertiary education.
  • Salary Packaging:
    • Novated lease for the purchase of a car
    • Salary packaging for personal IT equipment.
  • Contemporary offices:
    • Sit-stand desks and personal lockers
    • Free gym access and fitness classes in the building
    • Excellent end of trip facilities.
  
To find out more about the benefits of working at WATC, visit WATC’s Careers page.

How to Apply
WATC offer an inspiring and collaborative work environment where compliance is central to driving trust and innovation in financial services.
Join an organisation that is committed to employing highly skilled people, with diverse backgrounds and experiences that embraces diversity of all kinds including supporting Women In STEM.
You will have the opportunity to work within a supportive team that values excellence, transparency, and forward-thinking solutions. If you are seeking a role where you can make a tangible impact, apply now.

Only candidates with unrestricted working rights in Australia will be considered.

For further information please contact Emily Bulloch, Principal Consultant - Beilby Downing Teal on 0427 582 402 or ebulloch@beilbydt.com.au or click the link to download a copy of the Application Information Pack.
https://beilbydt.com.au/application-packs/
Please apply online at www.beilbydt.com.au by submitting a cover letter and resume (Word or PDF format) and quoting reference number 1251258.
Please note that applications will be assessed as they are submitted, so prompt submissions are encouraged.

job.title: Central Services Manager
job.description:
The Company

Join an established consulting engineering business that delivers practical solutions across construction and infrastructure projects. Working closely with its leadership and technical teams, you will help keep the business organised, well supported and ready for continued growth.

The Opportunity

The Central Services Manager will lead the day-to-day delivery of the business support functions. Reporting to the Managing Director, you will oversee finance administration, people processes, systems, facilities, compliance and business development support.

This is a practical, hands-on role for someone who enjoys improving processes, supporting others and making sure important tasks are completed accurately and on time.

Key Responsibilities
  • Lead and coordinate the finance, administration and business support team
  • Oversee invoicing, accounts, payroll inputs, budgets and monthly reporting
  • Manage recruitment coordination, onboarding, employee records and other people processes
  • Maintain compliance, insurance, contracts, policies and business records
  • Coordinate IT support, systems, offices, equipment and key suppliers
  • Support CRM, opportunity tracking, marketing and bid coordination
  • Improve workflows and move suitable administrative tasks away from technical staff
  • Provide clear updates, recommendations and reports to the leadership team
About You

This role will suit an organised and commercially minded manager who is comfortable working across different business functions and getting involved in the detail when needed.

We would like to speak with candidates who can demonstrate:
  • Experience managing business operations or shared services in consulting, engineering, professional services or another project-based environment
  • Experience across areas such as people operations, compliance, contracts, systems, facilities or supplier management
  • Strong organisation skills and the ability to manage competing priorities
  • Confidence using Microsoft 365 and business systems
  • Clear communication, sound judgement and a reliable approach to follow-through
Why This Role

Based in the heart of Sydney CBD, this is a broad role where you can make a visible difference to how the business operates. You will work closely with senior leaders, improve the support available to technical teams and help build strong foundations for future growth.

Please apply via the “Apply for this job” button or online at www.beilbydt.com.au. For further information, please contact Mark Turner on 0401 404 451.

job.title: Senior Corporate Financial Advisor
job.description:
About WATC

As the State’s central financial services provider, Western Australian Treasury Corporation (WATC) cares about the financial health of Western Australia’s government sector. WATC partner with government entities to achieve sound financial outcomes and provide access to a comprehensive range of corporate finance, debt and investment, risk management and foreign exchange products and advisory services. They also provide their investors with secure and sustainable opportunities.
You can find out more about the organisation including WATC’s purpose, history and key activities by visiting the About Us tab on the WATC website.

The Opportunity

Following continued organisational growth, WATC is expanding their Advisory Services team and are excited to offer an additional opportunity within the function. This role reflects their ongoing investment in building capability and supporting the organisation’s future growth and success.

This role of Senior Corporate Financial Advisor offers a unique chance to join a dynamic and growing team tasked with evaluating key projects that support the State’s long-term economic development. Working in an evolving environment, the successful applicant will liaise with clients across State agencies to facilitate the development of effective solutions tailored to address clients’ financial requirements.

WATC proudly supports flexible working practices and, as such, will consider full-time or part-time working arrangements for the right person.

Key activities: 
  • Developing and maintaining complex integrated financial models.
  • Conducting robust and considered financial evaluations and value-to-State assessments.
  • Undertaking research and analysis of drivers underpinning capital investment decisions, alternative financing structures, divestment decisions, financial valuations and procurement decisions.
  • Developing and implementing financial risk management strategies in line with client policy frameworks.
  • Provision of specialist investment appraisal advice and recommendations on investment prioritisation including strategic merit, maturity, benefit and cost of infrastructure, and
  • Assisting with the preparation of proposal papers, presentations, and government submissions.
You will also provide support to Principal Advisors in compiling and analysing financial information, and will contribute to the continuous improvement of internal processes and methodologies, training delivery and advocacy. The role also includes mentoring and developing WATC’s Corporate Financial Advisors to raise their skill levels towards the Senior Corporate Financial Advisor level over time.

About You

WATC is seeking positive and approachable individuals who enjoy working collaboratively, welcome the opportunity to mentor and share knowledge, and are passionate about being a part of the WATC advisory team. Your proactive approach and ability to remain agile in a dynamic environment will be key to your success in the role.

WATC’s ideal candidates will be critical thinkers who can demonstrate a combination of the following skills, qualifications and experience:
  • A tertiary qualification in finance, or a related discipline.
  • Experience in an advisory services environment.
  • Strong financial modelling skills.
  • Creative problem solving and analytical skills.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills within a client relationship and team context.
  • A high level of intellectual curiosity, and
  • A flexible, ‘can-do’ attitude to work.
WATC Values

WATC values shape our behaviours and define how we relate to each other, our clients and our community:

Integrity – We are open, honest and accountable. We adhere to the highest professional and ethical standards. We honour our promises.
Partnership – We work collaboratively with our stakeholders and colleagues towards achieving successful outcomes.
Adaptability – We challenge ourselves to think creatively and to continuously improve.
Achievement – We are engaged and focused on delivering valued outcomes for Western Australia.
Leadership – We use our knowledge and experience to contribute to the long-term benefit of Western Australia.

Employee Benefits
WATC offer a range of benefits beyond remuneration that include:
  • Flexible work arrangements:
    •  Excellent work / life balance
    •  Working from home options and flexible start and finish times
    • Compressed work schedules and part time work opportunities.
  • Health and wellbeing focus:
    • Calendar of a range of wellbeing initiatives
    • Two wellbeing days annually
    • Discounted health insurance.
  • Generous personal leave:
    • 12.5 days personal leave per year
    • Up to 12 weeks paid parental leave (on top of government paid parental leave scheme)
    • Access to purchase additional leave.
  • Diverse, inclusive and supportive work environment:
    • Strong organisational focus on diversity and inclusion
    • A range of staff initiatives to drive First Nations awareness and support women in finance
    • A reward and recognition program.
  • Professional development opportunities:
    • Training courses
    • Professional memberships
    • Structured learning opportunities.
  • Newly refurbished offices:
    • Sit-stand desks and personal lockers
    • Free gym access and fitness classes in the building
    • Excellent end of trip facilities.
   
To find out more about the benefits of working at WATC, visit their Careers page.

How to Apply

WATC offer an inspiring and collaborative work environment where compliance is central to driving trust and innovation in financial services.
